subject: DPA clarifications: controller/processor, subprocessors, breach timelines
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: DPA redline + a few clarification items

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Attached: DPA_v2_redline.pdf — this includes our standard processor-side edits (high level: liability carveouts, subprocessors, and notification language).
- Items you said you'd escalate to legal / wanted clarification on: controller vs processor roles, notification timeline for breaches, exact subprocessors list, and data residency/retention options.

Could you confirm whether Acme considers Redwood a processor in your model (I took notes that Acme will be the controller for patient PII)? If so, we can proceed with the attached DPA redline and propose a legal alignment call. 

Proposed next steps:
1) You review the redline and list any clauses you need tightened (controller/processor language, breach timing).
2) We share our subprocessors export and SOC 2 evidence links.
3) Book a 30-minute legal sync early next week if needed.

Attachments: DPA_v2_redline.pdf (PDF, redline)

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acmehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA redline + a few clarification items

Thanks Soojin — I reviewed the redline quickly and looped in our legal team (cc). A few clarifications we need before we escalate internally: 

1) Controller / Processor: Confirmed — Acme will be controller for patient records and decisions related to patient care. We need Redwood to accept the role of processor explicitly in the DPA and confirm you will act only on Acme's documented instructions.

2) Subprocessors: Please provide the full current list (company name + country) and your notification cadence for added subprocessors. Acme's policy requires either prior notice + opt-out for new subprocessors or a 30-day notification window.

3) Breach notification: Our security policy expects initial notification within 72 hours of discovery for incidents impacting PII; is Redwood able to commit to a max 72-hour initial notification window? If not, please explain typical timing and escalation practice.

4) Data residency & retention: For production patient workloads we must keep data in the US (primary), and retention for any logs containing PII must be configurable — default no longer than 90 days unless we opt-in longer. Also need confirmation around deletion procedures and certificate of deletion for terminated customers.

5) Evidence: please share SOC 2 Type II report and any penetration test summaries under an NDA link.

We also attached our standard DPA excerpt for reference (Acme_DPA_req.pdf). Will await your answers so we can route to legal.

— Emma
Emma Jones
Director, Cloud Integrations | Acme Health
emma.jones@acmehealth.com | +1 (718) 555-2229
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA redline + a few clarification items

Hi Emma — thanks for the thoughtful list. I'll address each item inline, and propose the next steps at the bottom.

1) Controller / Processor
- Confirmation: Per our standard DPA Redwood acts as "Processor" and Acme remains "Controller" for customer data and PII. We will add explicit language to the next redline reiterating we process only on documented customer instructions.

2) Subprocessors
- Attached: Subprocessors_20260510.csv (includes vendor name and country). High-level: our cloud infra provider, managed logging (optional), telemetry queues, and a small set of monitoring/security vendors.
- Notification cadence: we can offer a 30-day notification window for additions and maintain a public list that is updated in real time. If Acme requires a formal opt-out flow for a specific subprocessor, we can discuss alternatives (e.g., dedicated/private deployment or contractual restrictions).

3) Breach notification
- We aim to provide initial notification as soon as an incident is confirmed and actionable. Operationally our target is to provide preliminary notification within 48 hours of confirmation, with a subsequent incident report within 5-10 business days. For contractual language we can accept a 72-hour initial notification clause for incidents that reasonably impact PII, with the caveat that investigation timelines for complex incidents may extend the final report window.

4) Data residency & retention
- Residency: Hosted (shared) customers are served from US regions by default; Dedicated or Private deployments support strict US-only residency.
- Retention: Default log retention is 90 days; we can make retention configurable per-customer and offer deletion certification as part of offboarding/termination. We'll add explicit deletion process steps to the DPA appendices.

5) Evidence
- SOC 2 Type II: link (security portal) included below. We can provide our latest report under NDA. Pen test summaries are available; we can surface high-level results and provide a redacted summary to legal.

Next steps:
- I'll upload Subprocessors_20260510.csv and share the SOC2 link (see related links).
- Soojin — can you take the DPA_v2_redline and incorporate the controller/processor sentence + the 72-hour initial notice language we discussed, and circulate an updated redline?
- Emma / Acme legal — would you be available for a 30-minute sync on Thursday or next Monday to finalize language?

Attachments: Subprocessors_20260510.csv (CSV)
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/Redwood-Security-Evidence

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0137
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA redline + a few clarification items

Thanks Rishi — that helps a lot. We appreciate the flexibility on subprocessors and the willingness to add stronger breach timing language. A couple of quick items before we schedule legal: 

- Can you publish the Subprocessors_20260510.csv to your public subprocessor page and send the direct URL? We prefer a stable link our procurement team can reference.
- For the 72-hour clause, Acme legal will ask for explicit contractual language. If Redwood is comfortable with: "Provider will notify Controller without undue delay and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours of confirming the incident impacts Controller PII," that should let us move forward. Please confirm you can take that exact sentence (or equivalent) into the DPA redline.
- We will review SOC2 under NDA — please send the NDA link and access instructions.

If you can drop the updated redline by EOD today we will do a quick internal triage and propose a 30-minute timebox for legal alignment. Proposed times: Thu 11:00–11:30 PT or Mon 09:00–09:30 PT.

Attaching: Acme_DPA_req.pdf (our standard excerpt)

— Emma
Emma Jones
Director, Cloud Integrations | Acme Health
